description:
How Will Everything You Know End?

Episode 60 of a daily journey through the universe. 🌌
Season 3 finale: how will the universe end? The Big Freeze, where stars burn out over trillions of years and black holes slowly evaporate; the Big Rip; or a Big Crunch, which new hints about changing dark energy have brought back into the debate.

➡️ Tomorrow, Episode 61: Season 4 begins: the coldest place in the universe.
Start from Episode 1 "Leaving Earth" on the channel.
Follow so you don't miss a stop. A new episode every day.

#space #endoftheuniverse #astronomy #shorts #science

segments.text: How will the whole universe end? Scientists have three answers. None are comforting.
We've seen how the universe began. Now, the biggest question of all: how will it end?
segments.headline: How will it end?

segments.text: The universe is expanding, and dark energy is making it speed up. If that continues, we get the Big Freeze.
segments.headline: 1: The Big Freeze

segments.text: Galaxies drift so far apart that, from here, the sky beyond our local group of galaxies goes dark.
segments.headline: Galaxies drift away

segments.text: The smallest stars, red dwarfs, can shine for trillions of years. But eventually, even they burn out.
Then only black holes remain. And even they slowly evaporate, leaking away energy over unimaginable time.
segments.headline: Only black holes

segments.text: The last ones could take around ten to the power of one hundred years. A one, followed by a hundred zeros.
Option two: the Big Rip. If dark energy grows stronger, it could one day tear apart galaxies, stars, even atoms.
segments.headline: 2: The Big Rip

segments.text: Option three: the Big Crunch. If dark energy weakens, gravity could win, and everything could fall back together. Recent hints that dark energy is changing have made scientists take this seriously again.
segments.headline: 3: The Big Crunch

segments.text: Whichever it is, it's trillions upon trillions of years away. The universe is still young. And so is our journey.
segments.headline: The universe is young

segments.text: Season four starts tomorrow, with the coldest place in the universe. Colder than empty space itself. Which part surprised you most? Tell me in the comments, and follow for tomorrow's stop.
